findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In step 3, give each function's real return type and the fixture each one needs: an event JSON under `*/*.json` with an unrecognised top-level `event_type` (assert `_unknown_event_types_from_ref` returns it), a compat record with a non-null `epoch` and an `epoch_lineage` (assert the exact epoch or boolean), so that every site's assertion fails on the unfixed branch.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py:144-154: only candidates whose type isn't in known_types reach the `show` call
src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py:169: `return sorted(unknown)`

findings.finding: Approach step 3 says `_unknown_event_types_from_ref` and 'the 3 compat readers' 'return the committed content'. They don't. `_unknown_event_types_from_ref` returns a sorted list of unrecognised event types, and it only runs the per-file read when `git grep` finds an `event_type` outside KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES | _NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES. Committing ordinary event files would never reach the bridge_fsck site, so the test passes even without the fix. The compat readers return an (epoch, problem) pair (`_remote_store_epoch`) or booleans (`_remote_lineage_names`, `remote_epoch_supersedes_local`). On a failed read, `_remote_store_epoch` falls back to `rev-parse --verify` and returns (None, None), the same result as a tree with no record. So only an assertion on a real committed epoch can tell the fixed branch from the unfixed one.
findings.location: Approach step 3 ('`_record_at`, `_unknown_event_types_from_ref`, `_committed_toml`, the 3 compat readers and `_fixture_files` return the committed content')
scenarios: The fixture commits only known-type events, so the bridge_fsck read never runs and that site's fix goes untested on Windows.
The test asserts `_remote_store_epoch(...) == (None, None)` or doesn't commit an epoch. It then passes on the unfixed branch and doesn't cover that compat site.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'return the committed content' with per-function expectations: `_record_at` returns the committed record dict; `_unknown_event_types_from_ref` returns [<the committed unknown event_type>]; `_remote_store_epoch` returns (<committed epoch>, None); `_remote_lineage_names` and `remote_epoch_supersedes_local` return True for a lineage that names the (null) local epoch; `_committed_toml` returns the parsed table; `_fixture_files` returns ({path: content}, 0).

findings.finding: Approach step 1 argues equivalence only on exit code and stdout bytes. `git cat-file blob` and `git show` emit different stderr for a missing path or ref: cat-file prints `fatal: Not a valid object name <rev>:<path>`, while show prints `fatal: path 'x' does not exist in '<rev>'` or `unknown revision`. Show also distinguishes a missing ref from a missing path; cat-file collapses the two. The plan does not state that no site inspects stderr text or surfaces it in user-facing errors, or that no existing test asserts on that text.
scenarios: A compat reader distinguishes a missing ref from a missing path by matching 'does not exist in' and now takes the wrong branch
An existing unit test asserts the bridge_fsck / opcert error text contains show's message and fails after the swap
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to step 1: "No site branches on stderr text; sites that propagate stderr (bridge_fsck, _opcert_gate_config, check_complexity_baseline) will show cat-file's 'Not a valid object name' message, and no test asserts the old text (grep -rn 'does not exist in' tests/)."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove or correct 'the shape of `.tickets-tracker`' in step 3, explain why `--no-checkout` is used (real file paths stay under MAX_PATH), and note that readers of on-disk files (`_local_store_epoch`) see no local record, so the fixture must set up the epoch and lineage to match.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/init.py:301, :320, :338, :360: `_git(repo, "worktree", "add", tracker, branch)` / `-b` / `--orphan`, with no `--no-checkout`
grep for `--no-checkout` in src/rebar finds only completion_candidate.py:101
src/rebar/_store/compat.py:161-170, 291: `_local_store_epoch` reads `_record_path(tracker)` from disk, not the committed tree
findings.finding: Approach step 3 calls the `--no-checkout` linked worktree 'the shape of `.tickets-tracker`'. That's wrong: `rebar init` creates the tracker with a plain `git worktree add` (no `--no-checkout`), so the real tracker is checked out. The difference matters for the compat readers. `remote_epoch_supersedes_local` gets the local epoch from the record file on disk (`_local_store_epoch` → `_record_path`). In a --no-checkout worktree that file isn't present, so the local epoch is always None. The fixture has to plan for that, and it shouldn't be described as the production shape.
findings.location: Approach step 3 ('adds a `--no-checkout` linked worktree (the shape of `.tickets-tracker`)')
scenarios: The test author assumes the fixture matches production and asserts that `remote_epoch_supersedes_local` is True using a local epoch. But the local record isn't on disk, so the local epoch is None and the assertion fails on both the fixed and unfixed branches (or passes on both).
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'a `--no-checkout` linked worktree (unlike the checked-out `.tickets-tracker`, so no on-disk file passes MAX_PATH; on-disk readers such as `_local_store_epoch` therefore see no local record and the fixture's `epoch_lineage` must include null)'.
